original_goal: Approachable refined everyday clothing magazine; clear outfits, comfortable whole-film viewing, sustainable weekly production; later validate account growth with publishing results.
actual_difference_to_E02: Whole-film spatial/posture sequence: moving full outfit → same-look seated layer view → other-look seated layer view → moving full outfit. Cuts within one outfit establish an everyday moment. Not merely different standing poses or a concept rename.
history_caveat: Full→medium→medium→full ordering already used in Mira v2/D-related studies. Four shots, close/full ordering and dissolve are not new techniques. Proposed new viewing experience comes from lateral travel, seated clothing context and same-occasion shot relationships; difference must be judged in actual film.

observed_mechanisms: Same everyday outing links front walking, lateral travel, lower garment detail and a later seated rest.
Street/shop/tree locations have a role in the outing rather than arbitrary backgrounds.

representative_brackets.purpose: Front walking with full outfit around12.9-14.9s
Lateral travel and garment side around15.7-17.6s
Lower body/shirt and moving garment detail around26.6-29.5s

shots.framing: Native9:16 full person, visible head and shoes; camera chest-height/level/50mm view.
shots.scene: Quiet covered lunch-shop walkway by a plain window and fixed wooden bench; soft daylight from image-left.
shots.start: Model left of center in shallow front-three-quarter view, frontal readable face; front foot planted, trailing toe grounded; walking path remains inside frame.
shots.action: One or two ordinary steps diagonally toward image-right, no torso turn/cloth touch/camera approach.
shots.camera: Fixed; no zoom or simulated slowdown.
shots.clothing_information: Complete open cream blazer/white tee/navy straight trouser proportion and natural garment motion.
shots.end: Still moving slightly; do not wait for pose or look directly at viewer.
shots.required_still: New full-person movement-start image, not reuse the centered stance just for convenience.

shots.framing: Head to knees, comfortable front-three-quarter seated view; lapels/tee waist and bent trouser line remain visible.
shots.scene: Same window/bench/light; physically consistent photographed angle change.
shots.start: Already seated upright, feet supported on ground outside or within frame; shoulders relaxed, hands resting simply on thighs away from lapel/waist.
shots.action: One small natural torso lean toward the daylight, then relaxed settle. No full sit-down choreography.
shots.camera: Fixed chest-height relative to seated subject, level50mm view; different viewpoint is a cut, not an implied camera move.
shots.clothing_information: How open lapels, cotton tee neckline and trouser folds relate in a everyday seated posture. No comfort or fabric-performance claim.
shots.end: Head and chest near planned B1 entry position.
shots.required_still: New seated image derived from visually approved A1 wardrobe/scene lock plus approved identity anchors.

planned_dissolves.check: Scale changes plus seated height require joint storyboard review: face/lapel focus and light matched, not superimposed standing/seated bodies as a trick. If sustained double scale is uncomfortable, redesign adjacent view, do not shorten user dissolve or revert to rejected two-full version.
Same seated scale, head/waist and bench geometry; outfit changes only here. Not a comparison hook.
Maintain face/lapel viewing location and light; no jump in gaze direction. Standing/seated change must feel like montage, not magic standing-up.
